newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thumbnail sketches of potential Hong Kong leaders.
newsitem.headline: Thumbnail sketches of potential Hong Kong leaders.

text.p: The nomination period for the post of chief executive who will lead Hong Kong when Britain lowers its flag and hands the colony back to China at midnight next June 30, ended on Monday.

Here are sketches of the four people who have emerged as the frontrunners to succeed Governor Chris Patten -- and of the person the Hong Kong public supported but who ruled herself out of the picture.

The four candidates are engaging in campaign-style electioneering although the successful candidate, to be named in December, will be chosen by a China-appointed electoral college and not returned through the ballot box.

TUNG CHEE-HWA - Shanghai-born British educated business tycoon, Tung, 59, is a former member of Patten's inner cabinet, the Executive Council and a long-time adviser to China on Hong Kong affairs. He stepped down from the chairmanship of his family shipping empire Orient Overseas (International) Ltd in order to concentrate on his campaign.

Tung is a vice-chairman of China's Preparatory Committee (PC) responsible for the transition. He has strong contacts with China, Taiwan, Britain and the United States. He is widely seen as Beijing's favourite although he ranks only second favourite of the candidates in regular public opinion polls.

SIR TI LIANG YANG - Shanghai-born Yang, 67, resigned as Hong Kong's Chief Justice last month to run for the top job. He was knighted in 1988, when he became the first Chinese to head the Hong Kong judiciary under British rule. Yang's family moved to Hong Kong from China after the 1949 communist takeover. He is unpopular with the pro-democracy camp for remarks last year in which he attacked a Bill of Rights introduced by Patten against China's will.
Yang rates a point to two ahead of Tung in the opinion polls. Political commentators ascribe this to his lack of business links.
PETER WOO KWONG-CHING - Shanghai-born tycoon Woo, 50, is a son-in-law of late Hong Kong shipping magnate Sir Yue-kong Pao, a business rival of Tung's father.

The youngest candidate, Woo is a PC member and honorary chairman of Wharf (Holdings) Ltd and Wheelock and Co Ltd, but no longer engages in day-to-day running of his companies. In what many regard as the first step towards a career in politics, United States-educated Woo relinquished his business posts -- although he remains honourary chairman of the family business -- to concetrate on public service as the chairman of Hong Kong's Hospital Authority.

SIMON LI FOOK-SEAN - The Former Appeal Court Judge and member of one of Hong Kong's most prominent dynasties, Li was the last to enter the fray and has highlighted his local roots and status as the only leading candidate to have been born in the British colony. The oldest candidate at 74, Li was considered a contender for the post of Chief Justice awarded to Yang in 1988. Like Tung, Li is a vice chairman of the Preparatory Committee.

ANSON CHAN FANG ON-SAN - Shanghai-born Chan, aged 56, is Hong Kong's chief secretary, the most powerful civil servant and deputy to colonial Governor Chris Patten. The first woman to reach this post, the plain-speaking "iron lady" with a big smile is respected by civil servants for her integrity and administrative talent after 34 years in government service.

Described by a former civil servant as "the best man for the job" opinion polls show she is the preferred choice of Hong Kong people by far, but Chan declined to stand. She has expressed a willingness to stay on in her post and continue to serve Hong Kong.
